optional_context.comorbidity: mild dementia; hip fracture awaiting surgery, hospital day 2

reference_targets_freetext.item: Confusion Assessment Method (acute change, inattention via months backward, disorganized thinking, altered arousal)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Validated bedside diagnosis of delirium versus baseline dementia

reference_targets_freetext.item: Review MAR for opioids, benzodiazepines, anticholinergics, and any new drug in the last 24 h; ask about uncontrolled pain
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Medications and untreated pain are the most common reversible precipitants in a fracture patient

reference_targets_freetext.item: Infection source examination: lungs, suprapubic and costovertebral tenderness, skin and pressure areas, IV sites
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Low-grade fever with delirium demands a bedside source search before empiric treatment

reference_targets_freetext.item: Bladder palpation or percussion for retention and date of last bowel movement
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Urinary retention and constipation are frequently missed precipitants of delirium

reference_targets_freetext.item: Focal neurologic screen: gaze, facial symmetry, arm drift, speech
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Excludes a focal deficit that would reframe this as stroke rather than delirium

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask family or nurse for baseline cognition and time course, and ensure glasses and hearing aids are in place
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Establishes acuity of change and removes sensory contributors

off_bedside_acceptable: head CT only if focal deficit, fall, or anticoagulation
should_not_recommend: Haloperidol or benzodiazepine for agitation before delirium assessment and reversible-cause examination
Physical restraints as the first response
Head CT ordered as a substitute for bedside neurologic and delirium assessment
